change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an expression of concern on this paper, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached. Fig. 7 does not report LSD1 siRNA data, yet the paper states that LSD1 siRNA reduced H460 migration. Other noted issues are a possible discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 panel and insufficient control detail for replication. Similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results.
evaluation: In Section 3 your draft cites [12] for the H460 knockdown migration result and treats it as the clearest sign that LSD1 drives migration, while the stored paper reports that result. The notice says Fig. 7 does not report LSD1 siRNA data, so the result your Section 3 rationale rests on is not supported. In Section 2 your draft cites [12] for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue, which the stored paper reports; the notice questions the validity and provenance of the reported results but names nothing specific about this tissue finding. PLOS ONE issued an expression of concern about unresolved issues; the impact on your draft is medium, mainly through Section 3.
recommendation: PLOS ONE issued an expression of concern about unresolved issues. In Section 3, the draft cites [12] for the H460 knockdown migration result and calls it the clearest indication that LSD1 is a driver of migration, while the notice says the Fig. 7 figure does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the result statement is not supported. Hedge that sentence, cite the notice, and don't build Aim 2 on this result alone; look for independent support or run your own knockdown. In Section 2, the draft cites [12] for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue than in normal lung tissue, while the notice says similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Soften that background statement and cite the notice too. Tracking continues, so a retraction would raise a new alert.
